title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.35802v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many academic disciplines (in particular, mathematics and the theoretical sciences) face difficult questions about how to adapt their practices to the rise of highly capable artificial intelligence (AI). Before AI, a well-written research paper with a strong theoretical result acted as a reliable signal that its authors understood their field in depth. Now that AI is widely accessible, such signals have become cheaper to produce. As a result, they no longer reliably sort academics by their level of understanding. This has direct consequences for academic hiring. The age of AI raises a question for each side of the academic job market. Should an early-career researcher invest in a deep understanding of their field, or instead use AI to build a longer resume with many papers? translated_title: AI时代学术努力与招聘的博弈论
translated_abstract: 许多学科（尤其是数学和理论科学）面临着如何调整自身实践以应对强大人工智能（AI）崛起的难题。在AI出现之前，一篇具有强理论结果的优秀研究论文是其作者深入理解本领域的可靠信号。如今AI已广泛可得，这类信号的生产成本大大降低，因此它们不再能够可靠地区分学者对本领域的理解水平。这对学术招聘产生了直接影响。AI时代为学术就业市场的双方都提出了问题：处于职业早期的研究者应该投入精力去深入理解自己的领域，还是利用AI来打造一份包含更多论文的更长简历？招聘者应该青睐论文数量较少但通过了旨在考察理解深度的面试的申请者，还是坚持要求既有大量论文发表又通过面试？
tldr: 本文运用博弈论分析AI时代学术论文作为能力信号的价值贬值问题，探讨早期研究者应在“深入理解领域”与“借助AI大量发文”之间如何权衡，以及招聘方应如何设计甄别策略以挑选真正有理解深度的候选人。
en_tdlr: This paper applies game theory to analyze how AI devalues research papers as signals of deep understanding, exploring whether early-career researchers should invest in genuine understanding or use AI to build longer resumes, and how recruiters should design screening strategies in academic hiring.
